facts.title: Boats and capacity
facts.summary: Twenty boats with room for 1,178 people, for more than 2,200 on board.
facts.note: British report; the US report gives 1,176.

facts.title: Arrangement of the davits
facts.summary: Sixteen pairs of davits in four groups of four, forward and aft on each side. Odd-numbered boats were on the starboard side and even-numbered boats on the port side, numbered from forward.
facts.note: Report, Life-saving Appliances and Decks and Accommodation.

facts.title: The launching sequence is a reconstruction
facts.summary: No one recorded launch times during the night. Three modern reconstructions and the 1912 table disagree on the order and times of several boats. All four agree that No. 7 left first, at 12:40 to 12:45, and that the starboard forward boats left in the order 7, 5, 3, 1. The three modern reconstructions put collapsible C at 2:00 and collapsible D at 2:05 to 2:10; the 1912 table puts C at 1:40 and D at 2:05. Every time is approximate to about five minutes.
facts.note: The times shown follow Fitch, Layton and Wormstedt (2026); the other positions are attached to each boat.

alternatives.position: No. 6 before No. 8; aft port order 16, 12, 14, 10; starboard aft boats between 1:15 and 1:33.
Aft port order 10, 12, 14, 16; collapsible C at 1:40.

facts.title: Occupancy figures
facts.summary: About 712 people were saved in boats that could hold 1,178. The British report estimated that only about 652 can have left the ship in the boats, the rest being picked up from the water or transferred.
facts.note: Report, The Boats: the numbers claimed by witnesses total 854 and are called quite unreliable.

facts.title: Time taken to lower a boat
facts.summary: The launch times mark the moment a boat started down. The scene allows five minutes for a boat to reach the water unless a longer time is recorded, as for boats 1 and 6, which took about ten minutes.
facts.note: The five minutes are the project's assumption; no study read gives a typical lowering time.
